volumes.volume_summary_english: Volume 1 of Majmu'ah Kutub Ihtisab-e-Nasbiyat (Edited by Maulana Allah Wasaya, published by Aalmi Majlis Tahaffuz Khatm-e-Nubuwwat, Multan) comprises nine foundational classical and contemporary Sunni treatises (Books 1 to 9, pp. 13-472) refuting Nasibism (hostility toward the Ahl al-Bayt and apologetics for Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah). Beginning with a publisher's preface by Maulana Allah Wasaya (book pp. 4-12, PDF pp. 6-14), it features Imam Ibn al-Jawzi's famous 6th-century AH Hanbali refutation of Yazid's defenders (Al-Radd 'ala al-Muta'assib al-'Anid, both Urdu translation and original Arabic text), Imam Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti's collection of sixty hadiths on the virtues of the Prophetic Household (Ihya' al-Mayyit bi-Fada'il Ahl al-Bayt), and Hujjat al-Islam Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautawi's Persian and Urdu theological treatise on the martyrdom of Imam Husayn and the wickedness of Yazid. It further includes works by Hakim al-Ummat Maulana Ashraf Ali Thanawi on the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet's daughters, Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani's comprehensive historical monograph Shahid-e-Karbala, Maulana Mujahid al-Islam al-Qasimi's critical review of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's book Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid, two letters and a detailed fatwa by Shaykh al-Hadith Maulana Muhammad Zakariyya Kandhlawi on the Hadith of Constantinople (Maghfurun Lahum), and Mufti Sayyid Mahdi Hasan Shahjahanpuri's exhaustive research treatise Haqiqat-e-Yazid.

books.summary_english: This foundational 6th-century AH treatise by the celebrated Hanbali polymath Imam Ibn al-Jawzi (d. 597 AH) was written in response to 'Abd al-Mughith al-Harbi al-Hanbali's apologetic tract Fada'il Yazid. Preceded by an incisive introduction by Dr. Mufti Abdul Wahid and an extensive biographical study of Ibn al-Jawzi by the translator Mufti Muhammad Shuaib Ahmad, the work proves from the statements of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Qadi Abu Ya'la, and authentic historical reports that Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah was a flagrant transgressor deserving of condemnation and cursing. Ibn al-Jawzi documents Yazid's forced succession, his dispatch of 'Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad to massacre Imam Husayn and the Ahl al-Bayt at Karbala, the mistreatment of the Prophetic family in Kufa and Damascus, the sack of Medina during the tragedy of al-Harrah, and the catapult bombardment of the Ka'bah in Mecca. The book systematically dismantles every specious argument advanced by Yazid's defenders and concludes with the complete original Arabic text of Ibn al-Jawzi's treatise (pp. 165-188).

books.summary_english: Authored by the renowned Shafi'i hadith master Imam Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (849-911 AH) and translated into Urdu with Arabic text and source references by Mufti Shuaib Ahmad, this treatise compiles sixty Prophetic traditions establishing the exalted rank, love, and rights of the Ahl al-Bayt. Beginning with the Verse of Mawaddah (Qur'an 42:23) and the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, it gathers narrations from the Six Canonical Books, Musnad Ahmad, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and other collections demonstrating that love for the Prophet's family is a condition of faith while hatred or malice toward them is a sign of hypocrisy (nifaq) that leads to the Hellfire. It highlights the Prophet's special love for Fatimah, Ali, Hasan, and Husayn, the comparison of the Ahl al-Bayt to Noah's Ark, and the promise of Prophetic intercession for those who honor his progeny.

books.summary_english: Written by Hujjat al-Islam Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautawi (founder of Darul Uloom Deoband) as a detailed Persian epistle to Maulana Fakhr al-Hasan Gangohi and translated into Urdu by Prof. Maulana Anwarul Hasan Sherkoti, this work provides a rigorous theological and juristic analysis of Imam Husayn's martyrdom and Yazid's character. Presenting both the original Persian text (pp. 226-242) and full Urdu translation (pp. 243-268), Maulana Nanautawi establishes six foundational principles on consensus (ijma') and ijtihad before proving that Imam Husayn was superior in every qualification for the caliphate and that no valid consensus ever existed on Yazid's rule. He refutes the misuse of the hadith of the Constantinople expedition by showing that Mu'awiyah appointed Yazid while Yazid outwardly feigned uprightness, whereas after Mu'awiyah's death Yazid openly committed wine-drinking, adultery, tyranny, and the murder of the Prophet's grandson. He concludes by citing Qadi 'Iyad, Imam al-Nawawi, and the consensus of Sunni jurists, hadith scholars, and theologians on Yazid's wickedness (fisq) and the righteousness of Imam Husayn's stand.

Included in this encyclopedia to refute Nasibi polemicists (such as Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi and his followers) who denied that Sayyidah Zaynab, Ruqayyah, and Umm Kulthum were biological daughters of the Prophet, the work establishes the orthodox Sunni consensus on the honor and lineage of all four daughters alongside Sayyidah Fatimah al-Zahra.

books.summary_english: Authored by Grand Mufti of Pakistan Maulana Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani, this comprehensive historical and ethical work chronicles the tragedy of Karbala purely from authentic Sunni historical and hadith sources (such as Tarikh al-Tabari, Ibn al-Athir's al-Kamil, and Ibn Kathir's al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah). Beginning with the calamity of Yazid's nomination as crown prince and the principled refusal of the senior Companions in Medina and Mecca to pledge allegiance to a corrupt ruler, the book details Muslim ibn 'Aqil's mission and martyrdom in Kufa, Imam Husayn's journey toward Iraq, the blockade of water at Karbala, the negotiations with 'Umar ibn Sa'd, the night of worship before Ashura, the heroic stand and martyrdom of Imam Husayn and his seventy-two companions, and the fearless speeches of Sayyidah Zaynab and Imam 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin in the courts of Ibn Ziyad and Yazid. It concludes with an account of the divine retribution that befell every perpetrator of the massacre and an analysis of the supreme moral purpose of Imam Husayn's sacrifice.

books.summary_english: Written by the eminent Indian jurist Maulana Mujahid al-Islam al-Qasimi, this treatise provides a systematic critique of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's controversial work Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid. Al-Qasimi exposes Abbasi's methodological dishonesty in selectively quoting or distorting classical texts—specifically Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah and Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi's al-'Awasim min al-Qawasim—to portray Yazid as a pious ruler and Imam Husayn as a rebel. By reproducing Ibn Khaldun's full, unexpurgated Arabic passages alongside their Urdu translation, the author demonstrates that Ibn Khaldun explicitly declared Yazid a wicked transgressor (fasiq), affirmed that the Companions never approved of Yazid's actions, and established that Imam Husayn rose up to fulfill the obligation of resisting tyranny and died a noble martyr (shahid) while Yazid's forces sinned gravely in fighting him.

In the first letter to Maulvi Abdul Jalil, Maulana Zakariyya recounts how he immediately halted the reading of Abbasi's book in the gathering of the spiritual master Shah Abdul Qadir Raipuri and verified from Hafiz Ibn Hajar's Tahdhib al-Tahdhib that Abbasi had inverted the text: far from praising Yazid as trustworthy, Tahdhib al-Tahdhib records that Caliph 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz flogged a man twenty lashes for calling Yazid Amir al-Mu'minin and cites Imam Ahmad's ruling that hadith cannot be narrated from Yazid. The second letter records Shah Abdul Qadir Raipuri's emphatic declaration of devotion to the Sayyids (Ahl al-Bayt) and rejection of Abbasi's book.

books.summary_english: Originally published in the Deoband journal Monthly Tajalli (Rabi' al-Awwal 1384 AH), this treatise presents a ten-point questionnaire submitted by an apologist for Yazid regarding the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari ('The first army of my Ummah to invade Caesar's city is forgiven [maghfurun lahum]'), followed by Shaykh al-Hadith Maulana Muhammad Zakariyya Kandhlawi's point-by-point scholarly refutation. The questioner argued that the general wording of maghfurun lahum unconditionally guarantees Yazid's forgiveness for all past and future sins and objected to the conditions stipulated by hadith commentators such as Ibn al-Tin, Ibn al-Munir, al-Qastallani, Badr al-Din al-'Ayni, and Hafiz Ibn Hajar. Maulana Zakariyya demonstrates from the principles of Usul al-Hadith, Mulla 'Ali Qari's Mirqat, al-Bayhaqi, Qadi 'Iyad, and Ibn Taymiyyah that general glad tidings of forgiveness in hadith are always conditional upon eligibility, do not absolve subsequent major sins (kaba'ir) or violations of human rights (huquq al-'ibad) such as murder, and cannot be used to exonerate Yazid from the atrocities of Karbala and al-Harrah.

books.summary_english: Written by the head mufti of Darul Uloom Deoband's research department, Mufti Hafiz Sayyid Mahdi Hasan Shahjahanpuri, in reply to an inquiry from Sayyid Izhar al-Haq Suhayl Abbasi of Toba Tek Singh, this 74-page monograph is one of the most rigorous hadith and biographical (rijal) refutations of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid. First, the author authenticates the chain of narration in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib and Tarikh al-Khulafa proving that Caliph 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz flogged a man twenty lashes for calling Yazid Amir al-Mu'minin, and exposes Abbasi's blatant fabrications in attributing the praise of the narrator Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Ghaniyyah ('ahad al-thiqat') to Yazid. Second, he examines the fatwas of Imam al-Kiya al-Harrasi, Ibn al-Jawzi, Ibn Kathir, and Allama Anwar Shah Kashmiri on Yazid's wickedness and the tragedy of al-Harrah. Third, through chronological and historical analysis of the Byzantine campaigns (42-52 AH), he proves that Busr ibn Abi Artat—not Yazid—commanded the first army to reach Constantinople, and cites Hanafi jurists (Ibn al-Humam, Qasim ibn Qutlubugha, Qadi Thana'ullah Panipati) alongside the fatwas of Gangohi, Thanawi, Nanautawi, and Mufti Aziz al-Rahman.

volumes.volume_summary_english: Volume 2 of Majmu'ah Kutub Ihtisab-e-Nasbiyat (comprising Books 10 to 17, pp. 3-528, PDF pp. 4-529) presents eight major scholarly works by leading Sunni authorities of the Indian subcontinent refuting modern Nasibism and the ideological school of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi. It opens with Hujjat al-Islam Maulana Qari Muhammad Tayyib Qasmi's celebrated 150-page book Shahid-e-Karbala aur Yazid (Book 10), followed by textual critiques of Abbasi's fabrications by Maulana Aziz Ahmad Qasmi (Book 11) and Maulana Abu al-Manzur Shaykh Ahmad of Deccan (Book 12). The centerpiece of the volume is Book 13, Sayyiduna 'Ali wa Sayyiduna Husayn (pp. 177-396), written by the renowned historian Qazi Athar Mubarakpuri in response to Abbasi and summarized with appendices by Hazrat Sayyid Nafees al-Husayni. The final section of the volume (Books 14 to 17, pp. 397-528) brings together four works by Shahid-e-Islam Maulana Muhammad Yusuf Ludhianwi: a collection of detailed fatwas from Aap Ke Masa'il aur Un Ka Hal refuting Nasibi doubts regarding Sayyiduna 'Ali, Sayyiduna 'Abbas, Imam Husayn, and Yazid (Book 14); a refutation of Malik Sa'id Ahmad's pamphlet Sharh Hadith-e-Maghfur (Book 15); an extensive review of Maulana Qazi Mazhar Husayn's Kharji Fitnah exposing Maulana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi's alignment with Abbasi's circle (Book 16); and a sharp critique of Abdul Qayyum's Tarikh-e-Nawasib for falling into the opposite extreme of slandering Sayyiduna Mu'awiyah while claiming to refute Nasibism (Book 17).

books.summary_english: Authored by Maulana Qari Muhammad Tayyib Qasmi, long-serving Rector of Darul Uloom Deoband, with an introduction by his son Maulana Muhammad Salim Qasmi, this 150-page treatise is a landmark refutation of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid. Qari Muhammad Tayyib identifies and demolishes three core conspiracies ('mansube') in Abbasi's work: first, the attempt to strip Imam Husayn of his status as a Companion (Sahabiyyat) by questioning his birth date and Prophetic companionship; second, the attempt to portray Imam Husayn's refusal to pledge allegiance to Yazid as unlawful rebellion against an established caliph; and third, the distortion of the historical events of Karbala to absolve Yazid and his governors. Drawing on canonical hadith collections, classical biographical dictionaries (Usd al-Ghabah, al-Isabah, al-Isti'ab), and Sunni juristic manuals, the author proves Imam Husayn's exalted rank as a Companion and leader of the youth of Paradise, establishes the legal validity of refusing allegiance to an openly wicked tyrant, and thoroughly documents Yazid's tyrannical character and crimes.

books.summary_english: Originally published in Monthly Darul Uloom Deoband (January 1960), this incisive 18-page treatise by Maulana Aziz Ahmad Qasmi exposes six concrete examples ('namune') of textual tampering, truncation, and deliberate mistranslation committed by Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi in his book Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid. By placing Abbasi's quotes side by side with the original Arabic passages from Ibn Kathir's al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, Ibn Hajar's Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, and al-Dhahabi's Mizan al-I'tidal, the author demonstrates how Abbasi systematically deleted sentences that condemned Yazid's neglect of prayer and sensual indulgence, falsified the translation of Caliph al-Nasir's dialogue on cursing Yazid, falsely claimed Yazid was a trustworthy hadith narrator, and excised the statement of the hadith masters ('and he is the one who killed al-Husayn') from the biography of 'Umar ibn Sa'd.

books.summary_english: Published in Monthly Darul Uloom Deoband (January 1960) and later included as an appendix in Sayyid Nafees al-Husayni's edition of Sayyiduna 'Ali wa Sayyiduna Husayn, this 6-page review by Maulana Abu al-Manzur Shaykh Ahmad responds directly to Maulana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi Nadwi's controversial article in Sidq-e-Jadid (13 November 1959). Sandelvi had expressed astonishment that Sunni scholars—and especially Qari Muhammad Tayyib, Rector of Darul Uloom Deoband—were condemning Mahmud Abbasi's book as contrary to Sunni creed, claiming the book merely discussed historical events rather than religious beliefs. Maulana Abu al-Manzur demonstrates that Abbasi's book directly attacks foundational Sunni creed by maligning twelve centuries of hadith masters and historians (such as al-Tabari, Ibn Kathir, and al-Suyuti), slandering Imam Husayn with hadiths about dying a 'death of Jahiliyyah,' exalting Yazid above Sayyiduna 'Ali, and replacing the Rightly Guided Caliphs and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz with Umayyad monarchs as the twelve caliphs foretold by the Prophet.

books.summary_english: Originally serialized in 35 installments in the Bombay daily Inqilab (November-December 1959) by the eminent Indian Islamic historian Maulana Qazi Athar Mubarakpuri at the encouragement of Maulana Sayyid Muhammad Miyan Deobandi, and later abridged and edited in Pakistan by Hazrat Sayyid Nafees al-Husayni (December 2003), this 220-page work is a comprehensive historical and hadith refutation of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid. Restricting his rebuttal primarily to the very same classical sources that Abbasi had selectively misquoted, Qazi Athar Mubarakpuri exposes how Abbasi plagiarized Orientalist and Christian missionary distortions (such as Henri Lammens) while slandering classical Sunni imams. The book is divided into major sections covering the distinction between the Rightly Guided Caliphate and Umayyad monarchy, the legitimacy and universal acceptance of Sayyiduna 'Ali's caliphate (citing Shah Waliullah, Ibn Khaldun, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, and Imam Ahmad), the righteousness of Imam Husayn's stand against Yazid, the fabrications in 'Abd al-Mughith's Fada'il Yazid, the three atrocities of Yazid's reign (Karbala, al-Harrah, and the siege of Mecca), and detailed analyses of contested hadiths (the Constantinople campaign, Mulk 'Adud, Safinah's hadith of the thirty-year caliphate, and the twelve Qurashi caliphs), concluding with reviews from Darul Musannifin Azamgarh, Nadwatul Musannifin Delhi, and an exposition of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah's true stance.

The first major section (pp. 400-459) responds to two lengthy letters from a questioner who cited Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi's al-'Awasim min al-Qawasim and Sahih al-Bukhari to accuse Sayyiduna 'Ali and Sayyiduna 'Abbas of hiding during the Prophet's final illness, greedily disputing over the inheritance of Fadak and Khaybar, abusing one another in Caliph 'Umar's court, and seeking power after the Prophet's death. Maulana Ludhianwi lays down seven foundational principles on the reverence due to all Companions, thoroughly explains each hadith in context, and refutes every Nasibi insinuation against Sayyiduna 'Ali and Sayyiduna 'Abbas. The second section (pp. 460-472) addresses the contrasting status of Imam Husayn and Yazid, the permissibility of calling Yazid wicked (palid), the stance of Sunni elders on cursing Yazid, a rebuttal of two letters defending Yazid, and the reason why only the Four Rightly Guided Caliphs (together with Imam Hasan completing the thirty years) are included in the Khilafat-e-Rashidah.

books.summary_english: Originally published in the Karachi journal Monthly Bayyinat (Jumada al-Ula 1392 AH / July 1972), this 14-page treatise by Maulana Muhammad Yusuf Ludhianwi is a critical rebuttal of a 48-page pamphlet titled Sharh Hadith-e-Maghfur by Malik Sa'id Ahmad of Jhang (published by Maktabah Abu Mu'awiyah, Karachi). Articulating the balanced Sunni position between the two extremes of declaring Yazid an apostate and exalting him as a saintly hero over Imam Husayn, Maulana Ludhianwi explains that while Yazid remained within the fold of Islam and his ultimate fate in the Hereafter rests with Allah, his three-year reign is forever stained by the atrocities of Karbala, the massacre of Medina at al-Harrah, and the siege of Mecca. He further exposes how Malik Sa'id Ahmad fraudulently truncated Maulana Ahmad 'Ali Saharanpuri's marginalia on Sahih al-Bukhari (quoting Fath al-Bari) by deleting the refutation of al-Muhallab by Ibn al-Tin and Ibn al-Munir in order to fabricate the opposite meaning from the text.

books.summary_english: Published in Monthly Bayyinat (Rabi' al-Awwal 1404 AH / January 1984), this 28-page article by Maulana Muhammad Yusuf Ludhianwi reviews the 612-page work Kharji Fitnah (Part 1) by Maulana Qazi Mazhar Husayn of Chakwal, which was written in reply to Maulana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi Siddiqi's Izhar-e-Haqiqat and Jawab-e-Shafi. Maulana Ludhianwi summarizes six major proofs presented by Qazi Mazhar Husayn demonstrating Sandelvi's ideological alignment with Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's Nasibi movement: (1) Sandelvi's 1959 defense of Abbasi's Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid against Qari Muhammad Tayyib; (2) the inclusion of Sandelvi among Abbasi's disciples by 'Uzayr Ahmad Siddiqi alongside Hakim Fayz 'Alam, Abu Yazid Butt, and 'Azim al-Din; (3) Sandelvi's glowing endorsement of 'Azim al-Din's anti-Ali and pro-Yazid tract Hadithah-e-Karbala; (4) Sandelvi's denial that any Nasibi or Khariji group existed in Pakistan; (5) Sandelvi's characterization of Sayyiduna 'Ali's caliphate as merely 'provisional/emergency' ('uburi wa hangami) and his claim that Mu'awiyah was 'closer to the truth' (asahh) at Siffin; and (6) Sandelvi's endorsement of Tahir Makki's tract excluding Sayyiduna 'Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn from the Ahl al-Bayt in the Durud prayer. While fully endorsing Qazi Mazhar Husayn's doctrinal defense of Sayyiduna 'Ali's Rightly Guided Caliphate, Maulana Ludhianwi respectfully advises a gentler tone toward Sandelvi personally and notes Qazi Mazhar Husayn's critique of Maulana La'l Shah Bukhari's book Istikhlaf-e-Yazid.

books.summary_english: Originally published in Monthly Bayyinat (Rabi' al-Thani 1406 AH / January 1986) under the title Ek Nayi Kajrawi ('A New Deviation'), this concluding 14-page treatise by Maulana Muhammad Yusuf Ludhianwi critiques a book titled Tarikh-e-Nawasib (Part 1) by Abdul Qayyum B.A. of Rawalpindi. While ostensibly written to refute Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi and Nasibism, Abdul Qayyum fell into the opposite extreme of Rafidism by declaring Sayyiduna Mu'awiyah, 'Amr ibn al-'As, Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, and all Companions who sided with Mu'awiyah to be disbelievers and hypocrites (kafir wa munafiq), and by branding the greatest Sunni imams—including Imam Malik, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Imam al-Bukhari—as 'Nasibis' simply because they regarded Mu'awiyah as a Companion who erred in ijtihad (mujtahid mukhti) rather than a disbeliever or open fasiq. Citing Mujaddid Alf-e-Thani, Imam Abu Hanifah's Fiqh al-Akbar, Imam al-Tahawi's 'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Caliph 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, and the Prophetic hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari praising Imam Hasan's peace treaty with Mu'awiyah as a reconciliation between 'two great groups of Muslims,' Maulana Ludhianwi demonstrates that slandering the Companions in the name of refuting Nasibism actually serves the Nasibi cause and destroys Sunni orthodoxy.

volumes.volume_summary_english: Volume 3 of Majmua Kutub Ihtisab-e-Nasbiyat contains three seminal works (Books 18–20) by the premier hadith scholar of Pakistan, Shaykh al-Hadith Maulana Muhammad Abdul Rashid Nomani (1915–1999). Book 18, 'Nasbiyat Tahqiq ke Bhais Mein' (pp. 3–366), is an exhaustive posthumously published refutation of Mahmood Ahmad Abbasi's 'Khilafat-e-Muawiya o Yazid', dismantling Abbasi's reliance on Orientalists and non-standard books, his astronomical/calendar fabrications regarding Karbala, his slanders against Caliphs Uthman and Ali and Imam Husayn, and his falsifications of Shah Waliullah's writings. Book 19, 'Hadrat Ali aur Qisas-e-Uthman' (pp. 367–470), is a detailed juristic and historical response to Nasibi pamphlets in Karachi, proving from Sunni creed and hadith sources why Imam Ali could not immediately execute the rebels who besieged Uthman and exonerating Companions such as Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr and Amr ibn al-Hamiq. Book 20, 'Akabir Sahaba' (pp. 471–504), refutes Dr. Ahmad Husayn Kamal's pamphlet 'Hadrat Uthman ki Shahadat Kyun aur Kaise?' (published by Majlis-e-Uthman Ghani, Karachi), exposing its conspiracy theories against Banu Hashim and the senior Companions.

Maulana Nomani systematically exposes Abbasi's fabrications, reliance on Orientalists and unreliable works, mathematical and astronomical blunders in his tabular calendar ('Abbasi Jantari') regarding the days of the week in Muharram 61 AH, slanders against Caliph Uthman, Imam Ali, and Imam Husayn, false eulogies of Yazid, and deceptive truncations of Shah Waliullah's 'Izalat al-Khafa' and 'Qurrat al-Aynayn'.

Drawing upon 'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah', al-Jassas's 'Ahkam al-Quran', al-Bayhaqi, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Hajar, and Shah Waliullah, Maulana Nomani demonstrates the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah on the righteousness of Imam Ali in Jamal and Siffin, proves the Companionship and innocence of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr and Amr ibn al-Hamiq regarding Uthman's assassination, critiques Sayf ibn Umar's narrations, and explains the juristic reasons why Imam Ali could not immediately enforce qisas against the armed rebels.

volumes.volume_summary_english: Volume 4 of Majmua Kutub Ihtisab-e-Nasbiyat comprises nine works (Books 21–29) by leading Sunni scholars and eyewitnesses refuting modern Nasibism and pro-Yazid revisionism. Books 21–23 by Shaykh al-Hadith Maulana Muhammad Abdul Rashid Nomani refute the anti-Karbala pamphlet 'Dastan-e-Karbala Haqa'iq ke A'ine Mein' (Book 21), answer 12 pro-Yazid doubts raised by the Mahmudi/Abbasi group in light of Sahih al-Bukhari and classical Sunni authorities (Book 22), and document Imam Ali's unmatched foundational role in the Prophetic sciences and Hanafi jurisprudence (Book 23). Books 24–26 by the jurist Mufti Sayyid Abd al-Shakur Tirmidhi provide an incisive critique of Mahmood Ahmad Abbasi's 'Khilafat-e-Muawiya o Yazid' and 'Haqiqat-e-Khilafat o Mulukiyat'—exposing his rejection of nearly 900,000 hadiths, mockery of Sahih al-Bukhari, denial of Durood on Aal-e-Muhammad, and denial of Imam Mahdi (Book 24)—alongside treatises establishing the consensus of Sunni and Deobandi elders on Yazid's fisq against Azim al-Din Siddiqi (Book 25) and Ataullah Bandyalvi and Muhammad Husayn Nilwi (Book 26). Books 27–29 present firsthand personal testimonies by Hakim Sayyid Mahmood Ahmad Barkati, Grand Mufti Wali Hasan Tonki, and Musa Hasan exposing Mahmood Ahmad Abbasi's ignorance of Arabic, association with the hadith-denier Tamanna Imadi, insult of Sayyida Fatima al-Zahra, profanities calling Imam Ali an 'idiot', and refusal to recognize Caliph Uthman as the third Caliph.

books.summary_english: Written by Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain in April 1982 (Jumada al-Thaniyah 1402 AH) as an analytical preface to Mawlana Muhammad Qasim Nanautawi's famous epistle to Mawlana Fakhr al-Hasan Gangohi affirming the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (included as Book 4 in Volume 1). The treatise exposes the contemporary Nasibi and Khariji movement in Pakistan led by Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi (author of Khilafat-e-Muawiya wa Yazid) and his Karachi-based followers such as Maulvi Azimuddin, who disguised themselves behind Sunni and Deobandi labels while disparaging the Caliphate of Imam Ali and accusing Imam Husayn of rebellion. Qazi Mazhar Hussain also critiques Mawlana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi's endorsement of Abbasi's book, contrasting it with the orthodox Sunni path of moderation (Maslak-e-I'tidal) that unites reverence for all the Companions with devotion to the Prophet's Ahl al-Bayt. Drawing on Shah Waliullah Dehlavi, Mawlana Qasim Nanautawi, and Mawlana Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, the work urges Deobandi scholars not to collaborate with pro-Yazid Nasibi groups under the pretext of countering Shi'a polemics.

books.summary_english: Completed in September 1982 (Dhu al-Hijjah 1402 AH), this monumental 488-page treatise is Part 1 of Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain's comprehensive refutation of Mawlana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi's two-volume work Izhar-e-Haqiqat and his pamphlet Qazi Mazhar Hussain ke I'tirazat ka Jawab-e-Shafi. While Sandelvi ostensibly wrote Izhar-e-Haqiqat to refute Abul A'la Mawdudi's Khilafat wa Mulukiyyat, Qazi Mazhar Hussain demonstrates that Sandelvi fell into the opposite extreme of Kharijism and Nasibism by denying that Imam Ali was unequivocally on the truth (al-Haqq) in the battles of Jamal and Siffin, treating Imam Ali's Caliphate as merely 'interim' or disputed, and attacking classical Sunni authorities such as Imam Abu Bakr al-Jassas, Hafiz Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani, and Allama Anwar Shah Kashmiri. The author also documents the ideological nexus between Sandelvi and Pakistani Nasibi polemicists including Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi, Maulvi Azimuddin, Hakim Faiz Alam Siddiqi, Abu Yazid Butt, Aziz Ahmad Siddiqi, and Mawlana La'l Shah Bukhari. Citing Quranic verses (Surah al-Nur 24:55, Surah al-Hujurat 49:9), mutawatir hadiths ('Ammar will be killed by the rebellious group' and the thirty-year Caliphate of Prophethood), and verbatim texts from seventeen major Sunni authorities—including al-Baghdadi, Ibn Hazm, al-Isfara'ini, al-Ghazali, Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi, 'Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani, al-Nawawi, al-Marghinani, Ibn al-Humam, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani, Ibn Hajar al-Haytami, Mujaddid Alf-e-Thani, Mulla Ali al-Qari, al-Parharvi, and Mufti Muhammad Shafi—he proves the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah that Imam Ali was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph upon truth (Musib) while Amir Muawiya, though a respected Companion, committed an ijtihadi error (Khata-e-Ijtihadi) in opposing him.

books.author_english: Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain
books.summary_english: Completed in July–December 1986 (1406–1407 AH), this exhaustive 494-page volume constitutes Part 2 of Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain's refutation of Mawlana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi and the Nasibi-Khariji school, focusing specifically on the iniquity and transgression of Yazid ibn Muawiya (Bahs-e-Fisq-e-Yazid). Opening with an official fatwa from Darul Uloom Deoband endorsing his position against Mawlana La'l Shah Bukhari's Istikhlaf-e-Yazid, Qazi Mazhar Hussain systematically dismantles the pro-Yazid arguments of Sandelvi, Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi, Maulvi Azimuddin, and Shah Balighuddin across three major historical and theological axes: the martyrdom of Imam Husayn at Karbala (61 AH), the three-day sack and pillage of Medina at the Battle of al-Harrah under Muslim ibn 'Uqbah (63 AH), and the siege of Mecca and bombardment of the Ka'bah under Husayn ibn Numayr (64 AH). He exposes numerous textual fabrications by Nasibi writers—such as conflating the Kufan Tabi'i ascetic Yazid ibn Muawiya al-Nakha'i with Yazid ibn Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan, truncating Badr al-Din al-'Ayni's commentary on the Hadith of Constantinople ('Maghfurun Lahum'), and misquoting Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi, Imam al-Ghazali, Ibn Taymiyyah, and Mawlana Ashraf Ali Thanwi. Drawing extensively on Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Tarikh al-Tabari, Ibn Kathir's al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, Ibn al-Jawzi, Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah, Imam Abu Bakr al-Jassas, Mulla Ali al-Qari, Shah Waliullah, Shah 'Abd al-'Aziz, Mawlana Qasim Nanautawi, Mawlana Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, Mawlana Ashraf Ali Thanwi, and Mawlana Husayn Ahmad Madani, he establishes that Sunni orthodoxy unanimously regards Yazid as a fasiq (flagrant transgressor) and tyrant, while honoring the principled stand ('Azimah) of Imam Husayn and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr alongside the cautious patience (Rukhsah) of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.

books.author_urdu: حضرت مولانا قاضی مظہر حسین رحمہ اللہ
books.author_english: Hadrat Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain (rh)
books.summary_english: Completed in January 1985 by Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain (founder of Tehreek-e-Khuddam Ahl-e-Sunnat, Chakwal), 'Kashf-e-Kharijiyat' is a comprehensive 404-page polemical and theological refutation of 'Asal Haqiqat' (written under the name of Muhammad Ali Saidabadi to defend Mawlana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi's controversial book 'Mas'alah-e-Khilafat wa Imamat' against Qazi Mazhar Hussain's earlier critique 'Khariji Fitnah'). The author systematically exposes 37 specific fabrications and distortions ('lies') in Saidabadi's tract, defending his father Mawlana Karamuddin Dabeer's anti-Qadiani legacy and demonstrating through classical Sunni authorities (Imam Abu Hanifa, Ibn Hazm, Imam al-Nawawi, Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani, Mujaddid Alf-e-Thani, Shah Waliullah, and Shah Ismail Shahid) and contemporary Deobandi fatwas (Darul Uloom Deoband, Banuri Town, Darul Uloom Karachi) that recognizing Hadrat Ali (ra) as the rightful, divinely mandated fourth Caliph ('Muftarad al-Ta'ah') and viewing his opponents in Siffin as having committed an ijtihadi error ('Khata-e-Ijtihadi') is core Sunni orthodoxy. He further documents how Nasibi apologists like Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi influenced certain circles to demean Hadrat Ali (ra) and the Ahl al-Bayt under the guise of defending Hadrat Mu'awiyah (ra), while also critiquing Mawdudi and Khomeini to establish the balanced Sunni path of 'Haq Char Yar' and reverence for the Prophetic Household.

books.author_urdu: حضرت مولانا قاضی مظہر حسین رحمہ اللہ و مولانا حافظ عبدالحق خان بشیر نقشبندی
books.author_english: Hadrat Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain (rh) and Mawlana Hafiz Abdul Haq Khan Bashir Naqshbandi
books.summary_english: This book brings together two rigorous critical reviews—originally published in Monthly 'Haq Char Yar' (Lahore)—by Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Hussain (pp. 409–468) and Mawlana Hafiz Abdul Haq Khan Bashir Naqshbandi (pp. 469–512) refuting 'Waqi'a-e-Karbala awr Us ka Pas-Manzar' by Mawlana Atiq-ur-Rahman Sambhali (son of the prominent Indian Deobandi scholar Mawlana Manzoor Nu'mani). The authors expose how Sambhali departed from classical Sunni consensus and his own father's creed to act as an apologist for Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah and Ubaidullah ibn Ziyad, even including Mawlana Manzoor Nu'mani's published apology and disavowal of his son's disrespectful remarks regarding Imam Hussain (ra). Through detailed textual and historical analysis, the book refutes Sambhali's reliance on Ibn Khaldun and Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's Nasibi tropes, his false accusation that classical Sunni historians and imams were 'influenced by Shi'ism,' his whitewashing of Ibn Ziyad's brutality, and his audacious slanders against Imam Hasan (ra) and Imam Hussain (ra).

books.author_english: Shaykh al-Hadith Hadrat Mawlana Abdul Majeed Ludhianvi (rh)
books.summary_english: Originally delivered in January 2009 as a presidential address at a student speech competition at Jamia Siraj al-Uloom (Lodhran) and published in Volume 8 of 'Khutbat-e-Hakim al-Asr', this concise treatise by Shaykh al-Hadith Mawlana Abdul Majeed Ludhianvi outlines the orthodox Sunni doctrine regarding the virtues and rank of Sayyiduna Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra). Opening with Surah al-Hadid (57:10) and the Prophetic hadith comparing Imam Ali (ra) to Prophet Jesus (as) regarding whom two extreme factions went astray (exaggerators in love and Nasibi/Khariji haters), the author demonstrates how Imam Ali stands at the forefront of 'Al-Sabiqun al-Awwalun' (those who spent and fought before the Conquest of Makkah). While affirming the Companion status and respect due to Hadrat Mu'awiyah (ra), Mawlana Ludhianvi categorically establishes that Imam Ali (ra) is superior in rank and was closer to the truth ('Awla bil-Haqq') in their dispute, concluding with a sharp condemnation of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's 'Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid' and the Nasibi movement in Pakistan that disparages Imam Ali and the Ahl al-Bayt.

books.author_english: Hadrat Mawlana Muhammad Amin Safdar Okarvi (rh)
books.summary_english: Extracted from Volume 1 of 'Tajalliyat-e-Safdar' (pp. 536–548), this biographical and polemical treatise by the renowned Deobandi debater Mawlana Muhammad Amin Safdar Okarvi presents a comprehensive portrait of Sayyiduna Imam Hussain (ra) from authentic Sunni sources. Covering his noble lineage, birth, status as a Companion, physical resemblance to the Holy Prophet (saw), leadership of the youth of Paradise, and the immense reverence shown to him by the Rightly Guided Caliphs and Companions, the author simultaneously refutes the outrageous slanders of the Nasibi writer Hakeem Faiz Alam Siddiqui. The final sections chronicle Imam Hussain's principled refusal to pledge allegiance to Yazid, his martyrdom at Karbala, and the subsequent crimes of Yazid's regime—including the sack of Madinah (Harrah) and the siege of Makkah—citing Ibn Kathir's 'Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah' and the stance of Syed Ataullah Shah Bukhari.

books.summary_english: Selected from 'Tajalliyat-e-Safdar', this treatise contains Mawlana Muhammad Amin Safdar Okarvi's detailed open letter responding to Maulvi Zia-ur-Rahman Siddiqui Hazarvi's attempt to defend Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah. Okarvi clarifies technical terminology in 'Asma al-Rijal' (explaining that early Hadith critics applied the term 'Shia' to anyone who preferred Ali over Uthman, not to anti-Sahaba Rawafid) and proves that his indictment of Yazid rests entirely on authoritative Sunni classics such as Ibn Kathir's 'Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah', Shah Waliullah, and Shah Abdul Aziz Dehlavi's 'Fatawa Azizi'. books.summary_english: Taken from Volume 1 of 'Tajalliyat-e-Safdar' (pp. 579–594), this open letter was written by Mawlana Muhammad Amin Safdar Okarvi in reply to Mawlana Muhammad Amin Orakzai of Hangu (Kohat district), who had objected to Okarvi's Muharram article in Monthly 'Al-Khair' (Multan) condemning Yazid. Okarvi frames the fundamental theological dilemma: since Imam Hussain (ra), Abdullah ibn Zubayr (ra), and the Companions of Madinah opposed Yazid, exonerating Yazid as a 'just caliph' would mean condemning those noble Companions as rebels. He compiles explicit verdicts from eleven supreme Sunni and Deobandi authorities—including Mujaddid Alf-e-Thani, Shah Waliullah, Shah Abdul Aziz, Qasim Nanautawi, Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, Ashraf Ali Thanwi, Hussain Ahmad Madani, Abdul Shakoor Lakhnawi, Qari Muhammad Tayyib, Yusuf Banuri, and Mufti Muhammad Shafi—all affirming Yazid's wickedness (Fisq). He also refutes every standard pro-Yazid argument, including the Constantinople hadith (proving chronologically that Yazid was not in the first raiding army), the report attributed to Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, and the testimony of Abdullah ibn Hanzalah.

books.summary_english: Originally published in Volume 1 of 'Tajalliyat-e-Anwar' (pp. 286–336) following an exchange in Monthly 'Al-Khair' (Multan, 1425 AH), this 50-page treatise by Mufti Muhammad Anwar Okarvi (Head of Da'wah and Irshad at Jamia Khair al-Madaris, Multan) provides a point-by-point refutation of an apologist who attempted to defend Yazid under the pretext of defending Hadrat Mu'awiyah (ra) and critiquing Qazi Mazhar Hussain. The author demonstrates from classical theological and historical texts (including Taftazani's 'Sharh al-Aqa'id', Ibn Hajar al-Haytami's 'Al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqah', Shah Waliullah, and Mujaddid Alf-e-Thani) that distinguishing between the noble Companion Hadrat Mu'awiyah (ra) and his tyrannical son Yazid is essential to Sunni orthodoxy. He thoroughly examines the coercive nature of Yazid's nomination, refutes the fabricated story that Imam Hussain (ra) offered to pledge allegiance to Yazid at Karbala, analyzes Ibn Taymiyyah's actual position, proves that Yazid cannot be included in the Hadith of the Twelve Caliphs, and clarifies the Sunni rulings on declaring Yazid a Fasiq (transgressor) and cursing him.

books.summary_english: Selected by the renowned scholar and calligrapher Sayyid Nafees al-Hussaini from Professor Mawlana Sayyid Abu Bakr Ghaznavi's celebrated book 'Qurbat ki Rahein' (Paths of Nearness to Allah), this deeply moving essay expounds upon love for the Prophetic Household (Ahl al-Bayt) as an indispensable requirement of faith. Drawing on classical Arabic poetry, the Companions' intense devotion to every relic connected to the Holy Prophet (saw), the Qur'anic verses of Purification (33:33) and Salawat (33:56), and authentic Prophetic traditions in Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Musnad Ahmad, and Jami' al-Tirmidhi (including Hadith al-Thaqalayn and the Hadith of Noah's Ark), Ghaznavi illustrates the supreme station of Sayyiduna Hasan and Sayyiduna Hussain (ra) and the reverence shown to them by Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and the Companions. He concludes with a powerful rebuke of contemporary Nasibi-inclined preachers who mount the pulpits of the Prophet (saw) only to disparage the beloved grandson of the Prophet (saw) as though acting as defense attorneys for Shimr, Yazid, and Ibn Ziyad.

books.author_urdu: مولانا محمد یوسف لدھیانوی رحمہ اللہ فاضل دیوبند (ٹوبہ ٹیک سنگھ)
books.author_english: Mawlana Muhammad Yusuf Ludhianvi (rh) of Toba Tek Singh (Graduate of Darul Uloom Deoband)
books.summary_english: Written in 1960 by Mawlana Muhammad Yusuf Ludhianvi of Toba Tek Singh (an elder Deobandi scholar distinct from the later martyr of Karachi) when a local preacher began propagating Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi's notorious Nasibi work 'Khilafat-e-Mu'awiyah wa Yazid', this 266-page book is one of the most exhaustive scholarly refutations of Abbasi's thesis. The author systematically defends the legitimacy and consensus of Hadrat Ali al-Murtada's (ra) Caliphate against Abbasi's distortions, explains the historical causes of the disputes among the Companions, and establishes the Shar'i justification of Imam Hussain's (ra) refusal to pledge allegiance to Yazid. He subjects Yazid's life and rule to the touchstones of Hadith and history—covering the tragedy of Karbala, the massacre of Madinah (Harrah), and the siege of Makkah—while demolishing Abbasi's misuse of the Constantinople hadith, the Hadith of the Twelve Caliphs, the report of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, and Caliph al-Mansur's letter. The book also incorporates a major research treatise by Mawlana Muhammad Qasim Nanautawi (founder of Darul Uloom Deoband) on Karbala and Yazid, a survey of classical Sunni verdicts from the Four Imams to Mujaddid Alf-e-Thani and Shah Waliullah, and official fatwas from Darul Uloom Deoband and the scholars of Karachi condemning Abbasi's book.

books.title_translit: Maqam-e-Ahl-e-Bayt-e-Kiram (ra) ('Aqidat al-Islam fi Manaqib Ahl al-Bayt al-Kiram)
books.title_english: The Status of the Noble Ahl al-Bayt (ra) (The Creed of Islam Regarding the Virtues of the Noble Household)
books.author_urdu: علامہ ڈاکٹر خالد محمود رحمہ اللہ (مانچسٹر) و مولانا حافظ محمد اقبال رنگونی
books.author_english: Allama Dr. Khalid Mahmood (rh) (Manchester) and Mawlana Hafiz Muhammad Iqbal Rangooni
books.summary_english: Compiled and introduced by Mawlana Hafiz Muhammad Iqbal Rangooni (Editor of Monthly 'Al-Hilal', Manchester) around the seminal treatise of his teacher Allama Dr. Khalid Mahmood (Director of the Islamic Academy, Manchester and former Justice of the Supreme Court of Pakistan), this 98-page work expounds the orthodox Sunni theology of love and reverence for the Prophetic Household (Ahl al-Bayt). Describing the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt as 'the two eyes of faith,' the authors establish from Qur'anic verses, canonical Hadith collections, and classical authorities (Mujaddid Alf-e-Thani, Shah Waliullah Dehlavi, Qazi Thanaullah Panipati, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Abidin al-Shami) that love for the Ahl al-Bayt—encompassing both the Mothers of the Believers and the Ahl al-Kisa (Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Hussain) and their righteous progeny—is among the essentials of Sunni Islam. The book also highlights how the Twelve Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, such as Imam Muhammad al-Baqir and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, were revered Sunni legal and spiritual masters ('A'immah-e-Wilayat') and refutes Nasibi attempts to deny the continuity or sanctity of the Sadat lineage.

books.summary_english: Extracted from the book 'Fahm-e-Hadith' (Understanding Hadith) by the prominent jurist and Hadith scholar of Jamia Madania (Lahore), Dr. Mufti Abdul Wahid (rh), this concise 14-page compendium presents the primary Qur'anic verses and authentic Prophetic traditions on the personal virtues of the Prophetic Household, accompanied by clear Urdu translations and explanatory notes ('Fa'idah'). It covers the Qur'anic honor of the Mothers of the Believers (Surah al-Ahzab), the specific virtues of Sayyidah Khadijah al-Kubra (ra) and Sayyidah 'A'ishah al-Siddiqah (ra), the inclusion of Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Hussain (ra) in the Verse of Mubahalah (3:61), and the canonical hadiths from Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Jami' al-Tirmidhi, and Musnad Ahmad establishing the exalted merits of Hadrat Ali al-Murtada (including Hadith al-Manzilah, the Banner of Khaybar, and Ghadir Khumm), Sayyidah Fatima al-Zahra, and the two masters of the youth of Paradise, Imam Hasan and Imam Hussain (including Hadith al-Thaqalayn and the Hadith of Noah's Ark).

books.title_translit: Al-Durr al-Thamin fi Difa' Mawlana Muhammad Amin
books.title_english: The Precious Pearl in Defense of Mawlana Muhammad Amin (Safdar Okarvi)
books.author_urdu: شیخ الحدیث حضرت مولانا منیر احمد منور مدظلہم
books.author_english: Shaykh al-Hadith Mawlana Munir Ahmad Munawwar
books.summary_english: This comprehensive polemical and legal treatise by Shaykh al-Hadith Mawlana Munir Ahmad Munawwar defends the renowned Deobandi debater Mawlana Muhammad Amin Safdar Okarvi against deceptive accusations orchestrated by contemporary Nasibis and Yazid-apologists (specifically Abdul Wajid Latif and followers of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi and Qazi Tahir al-Hashimi). The detractors had submitted a manipulative legal query (istifta') to Dar al-Uloom Deoband without naming Mawlana Okarvi,cherry-picking two historical narrations from Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah that Okarvi had cited polemically regarding Mu'awiyah's appointment of Yazid, in order to accuse Okarvi of disrespecting Sayyiduna Mu'awiyah. Mawlana Munawwar presents endorsements from thirteen major Dar al-Ifta' institutions (including Dar al-Uloom Deoband, Mazahir Uloom Saharanpur, Dar al-Uloom Haqqaniyyah, and Jamia Khayr al-Madaris) and thirteen prominent scholars, proving that Mawlana Okarvi was a staunch defender of Sayyiduna Mu'awiyah and the Companions while maintaining the orthodox Sunni consensus on Yazid's transgression (fisq). The book systematically outlines the beliefs of Rafidis, Nasibis, and Ahl al-Sunnah, summarizes forty-one classical and Deobandi scholarly testimonies on Yazid's character, refutes ten common pro-Yazid doubts, poses seventeen pointed questions to Nasibis, and provides a rigorous hadith and rhetorical analysis of the two contested narrations from Ibn Kathir.

books.summary_english: Originally compiled as part of the biographical notes in 'Biya ba-Majlis-e-Nafis' (the discourses of Sayyid Nafis al-Husayni, spiritual successor of Shah 'Abd al-Qadir Raipuri) and subsequently expanded into a standalone treatise, this work by Mawlana Naeem al-Din (Professor of Hadith at Jamia Madaniyyah, Lahore) presents a concise, well-documented Sunni assessment of Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah's life, moral character, and rule. Drawing upon classical historical and hadith sources such as Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, Ibn al-Athir's Al-Kamil, and Suyuti's Tarikh al-Khulafa', the author outlines the three major atrocities of Yazid's तीन-year reign: the martyrdom of Imam Husayn at Karbala (61 AH), the sack of Medina at the Battle of Harrah (63 AH), and the siege and bombardment of the Ka'bah in Mecca (64 AH). The treatise then refutes the two primary arguments used by modern Yazid-apologists—the hadith of the first army to attack Caesar's city (Bukhari) and the pledge of allegiance by certain Companions—while concluding with a defense of Sayyiduna Mu'awiyah's integrity and good intentions in light of Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah.

books.summary_english: Authored by the prominent Deobandi theologian Mawlana Muhammad Ilyas Ghumman, this 206-page monograph provides an exhaustive Sunni biography and defense of Sayyiduna Husayn ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both). Divided into three comprehensive parts, Part One documents Imam Husayn's birth, prophetic upbringing, physical and moral resemblance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), immense canonical virtues, devotion to worship, and deeply affectionate relationships with the Rightly Guided Caliphs (Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, and 'Ali) as well as Sayyiduna Mu'awiyah and other Companions. Part Two chronicles the complete historical trajectory of the tragedy of Karbala—from Yazid's accession, Husayn's departure from Medina to Mecca and toward Kufah, the martyrdom of Muslim ibn 'Aqil, the confrontation at Karbala, the martyrdom of Husayn and his family on 10 Muharram 61 AH, to the aftermath in Kufah and Damascus—identifying eight principal culprits including the Kufan traitors, 'Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, Shimr, 'Umar ibn Sa'd, and Yazid himself. Part Three systematically refutes twelve major objections raised by Nasibis and modern skeptics (such as denying Husayn's Sahabi or Ahl al-Bayt status, accusing him of rebellion, or denying the historical reality of Karbala) as well as sectarian excesses regarding mourning.

books.summary_english: Written by Dr. Mohsin Usmani Nadwi (formerly Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi) with a foreword by Mawlana Sayyid Abu al-Hasan 'Ali Nadwi, this analytical treatise originally served as the scholarly introduction to an Indian collection of three anti-Nasibi works by Mawlana Muhammad 'Abd al-Rashid Nomani. The book examines the theological, political, and ideological background of the tragedy of Karbala, contrasting the Rightly Guided Caliphate with the hereditary monarchy introduced by Yazid's nomination. While affirming the honor and ijtihad of Sayyiduna Mu'awiyah and the Companions, Dr. Nadwi demonstrates how Imam Husayn's stand represented the pinnacle of prophetic resolve ('azimah) against an unrighteous ruler, citing the legal and theological positions of Imam Abu Hanifah, Imam Malik, Abu Bakr al-Jassas, Imam al-Ghazali, Imam al-Juwayni (Imam al-Haramayn), Ibn Hazm, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani, and Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani (Sharh al-'Aqa'id al-Nasafiyyah). It concludes with a penetrating psychological diagnosis of three modern maladies that drive certain writers to minimize Karbala or defend Yazid: a secularized reduction of Islam to private rituals divorced from political justice, an overreaction against Shi'ism that empties the heart of love for the Ahl al-Bayt, and Western-influenced hyper-rationalism devoid of prophetic love ('ishq-e-Rasul).

books.summary_english: Written in 1402 AH by Mawlana Mufti Sher Muhammad Alawi as a scholarly introduction to Mawlana Muhammad Qasim Nanautawi's famous epistle on the martyrdom of Imam Husayn and the transgression of Yazid (published as Book 3 in this encyclopedia, with a preface by Mawlana Qazi Mazhar Husayn as Book 30), this 14-page treatise compiles seventeen authoritative classical and Deobandi testimonies establishing the Sunni consensus on Yazid's fisq (open transgression and tyranny). Mufti Alawi directly refutes Mawlana Muhammad Ishaq Sandelvi Nadwi (author of Jawab-e-Shafi) and Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi, who broke with fourteen centuries of Sunni scholarship by calling Yazid a 'just caliph' (khalifah 'adil). books.title_english: The Character of Marwan ibn al-Hakam in the Mirror of Critical Research: A Technical and Scholarly Evaluation of Hadith and Historical Narrations Regarding Marwan in Light of 'Ilm al-Rijal
books.author_urdu: حضرت مولانا محمد اسماعیل ریحان مدظلہم
books.author_english: Mawlana Muhammad Ismail Rehan
books.summary_english: This monumental 448-page critical monograph by the contemporary Deobandi historian Mawlana Muhammad Ismail Rehan (author of Tarikh-e-Ummat-e-Muslimah) subjects the life, status, and political career of the Umayyad ruler Marwan ibn al-Hakam (d. 65 AH) to rigorous evaluation through the classical sciences of hadith criticism ('ilm al-rijal) and historiography. Written to counter modern Nasibi and Marwanite revisionists (followers of Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi) who attempt to elevate Marwan to the status of a Companion (Sahabi) or infallible authority while dismissing all critical reports as Shi'a fabrications, the author relies exclusively on Sunni canonical hadith collections (such as Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Musnad Ahmad, and Mustadrak al-Hakim) and classical Sunni masters of jarh wa ta'dil (including al-Bukhari, Ibn Hajar, al-Dhahabi, Ibn Kathir, al-Sakhawi, and Shah 'Abd al-'Aziz Dihlavi). Across eight detailed chapters and an appendix answering twelve Marwanite apologetic arguments, Mawlana Rehan proves that Marwan was born after the Hijrah, never saw the Prophet at an age of discernment, was exiled to Ta'if with his father al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As, is categorized as a Tabi'i of disputed reliability rather than a Sahabi, and committed grave offenses—foremost among them killing the Companion Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah at the Battle of the Camel, usurping the caliphate by force at Marj Rahit, altering the Sunnah of the 'Eid sermon, and instituting the Umayyad practice of reviling Sayyiduna 'Ali from the pulpits—while clarifying why Sayyiduna 'Uthman cannot be blamed for Marwan's later actions and why Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Malik recorded a handful of his legal reports with corroborating chains.

books.summary_english: This scholarly monograph by Mufti Muhammad Zahid (Shaykh al-Hadith at Jamia Islamia Imdadia, Faisalabad) establishes the theological and political legitimacy of the Caliphate of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) and his righteousness in the civil wars (Jamal, Siffin, and Nahrawan) strictly through authentic Prophetic Hadiths. Writing in response to contemporary Nasibi currents that cast doubt on whether Ali (RA) was one of the rightly-guided Rashidun Caliphs or portray his era as the root of Islamic tribulations (fitan), the author analyzes the Hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, the Hadith of Safinah on the thirty-year Prophetic Caliphate, the Hadith of Ghadir Khumm, and the Prophetic prophecies regarding Ammar ibn Yasir being killed by the rebellious party (al-fi'ah al-baghiyah) and the fighting against the Khawarij. He demonstrates that the Salaf—including Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Aisha, Talhah, Zubayr, and Abdullah ibn Umar—unanimously recognized Ali's (RA) rightful caliphate while maintaining the orthodox Sunni etiquette regarding the disputes among the Companions (Mushajarat-e-Sahaba). Primary sources cited extensively include Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Musnad Ahmad, Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Mustadrak al-Hakim, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah, and Shah Abdul Aziz Dehlavi's Tuhfah Ithna Ashariyyah.

books.title_english: Defense of Hazrat Hussain (RA): A Critical Examination of the Objections Raised by the Partisans of Yazid
books.author_urdu: حافظ عبد الجبار سلفی مدظلہم (مرتب: محمد عثمان حسن)
books.author_english: Hafiz Abdul Jabbar Salafi (Compiled by Muhammad Usman Hasan)
books.summary_english: Originally serialized in fifty installments under the title 'Yazidi Fitnah' in the monthly journal Haq Char Yar (Lahore) beginning in August 2009, this comprehensive polemical work by Hafiz Abdul Jabbar Salafi systematically refutes modern South Asian pro-Yazid (Nasibi) authors and pamphleteers. The author critiques writers such as Mahmud Ahmad Abbasi, Abu Yazid Muhammad Din Butt, Azeemuddin Siddiqui, Uzair Ahmad Siddiqui, Nazir Ahmad Shakir, and Hakim Muhammad Idris Farooqi, exposing their textual distortions and attacks on Imam Hasan, Imam Hussain, and classical Sunni authorities like Allamah al-Taftazani. Key theological and historical discussions include proving that the Hadith of Constantinople ('Maghfurun Lahum') applies to Amir Muawiyah's naval expedition rather than Yazid, documenting Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's punishment of anyone calling Yazid 'Amir al-Mu'minin', analyzing the terms of Imam Hasan's peace treaty, and demonstrating the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah on Yazid's sinfulness (fisq) and tyranny at Karbala and Harrah. The work draws heavily upon Fath al-Bari, Irshad al-Sari, Ibn al-Jawzi's Al-Radd ala al-Muta'assib al-Anid, Ibn Taymiyyah's Minhaj al-Sunnah, and Ali Hujwiri's Kashf al-Mahjub.

books.title_translit: Yazid Akabir Ulama-e-Ahl-e-Sunnat Deoband Ki Nazar Mein
books.title_english: Yazid in the View of the Senior Scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah Deoband
books.author_urdu: مولانا قاری محمد ضیاء الحق صاحب اور میاں رضوان نفیس
books.author_english: Maulana Qari Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq and Mian Rizwan Nafees
books.summary_english: This documentary compendium compiled by Qari Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq and expanded by Mian Rizwan Nafees presents verbatim fatwas, exegetical comments, hadith lectures, and historical writings of over eighty foundational and contemporary scholars of the Deobandi school of Sunni Islam regarding Yazid ibn Muawiyah. Divided into two parts preceded by twenty-seven scholarly endorsements (including Mufti Muhammad Taqi Usmani, Qari Muhammad Hanif Jalandhari, and Sayyid Muhammad Shahid Saharanpuri), the book demonstrates the unbroken consensus of the Akabir of Deoband that Yazid was a wicked transgressor (fasiq wa fajir) responsible for the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (RA) and the desecration of Medina. Featured authorities include Maulana Muhammad Qasim Nanautawi, Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, Ashraf Ali Thanwi, Mahmud Hasan Deobandi, Khalil Ahmad Saharanpuri, Anwar Shah Kashmiri, Hussain Ahmad Madani, Mufti Kifayatullah Dehlavi, Mufti Muhammad Shafi, Qari Muhammad Tayyib, Muhammad Yusuf Banuri, Zakariyya Kandhlawi, Abdur Rashid Nomani, and Sarfaraz Khan Safdar. It serves as an authoritative reference refuting anyone who falsely attributes pro-Yazid sympathies to the Deoband tradition.

books.author_urdu: حضرت مولانا مجیب الرحمن ڈیروی صاحب
books.author_english: Maulana Mujeeb-ur-Rehman Dardvi (Dera Ismail Khan)
books.summary_english: Authored by Maulana Mujeeb-ur-Rehman Dardvi of Darul Uloom Islamia (Dera Ismail Khan), this treatise critically examines the biography and status of the Umayyad ruler Marwan ibn al-Hakam, written in direct refutation of Qazi Tahir Ali Hashmi's apologetic book 'Sayyiduna Amir Marwan ibn al-Hakam: Shakhsiyyat aur Kirdar'. Using principles of Usul al-Hadith and biographical dictionaries (Ilm al-Rijal), the author proves that Marwan is not a Companion (Sahabi) because he never attained mature sighting of the Prophet (PBUH) and himself admitted to only being a Tabi'i, carefully contextualizing citations from Ibn Hajar's Al-Isabah, Ibn Abd al-Barr's Al-Isti'ab, and Al-Dhahabi's Siyar A'lam al-Nubala. Furthermore, the book documents from authentic Sunni chains Marwan's killing of the Companion Talhah ibn Ubaydullah (RA) during the Battle of Jamal, his armed rebellion against the rightful Caliph Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA), his obstruction of Imam Hasan's (RA) burial near the Prophet's chamber, his alteration of the Eid sermon sunnah, and his documented hostility (Nasibism) toward Imam Ali, Hasan, and Hussain (RA) as recorded by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ibn Hajar al-Haytami.

books.title_english: The Case of Imam Hussain (RA): The Incident of Karbala and the Character of Yazid in the Light of Authentic Narrations, and a Refutation of Nasibi Arguments
books.author_urdu: جناب علی طحاوی صاحب
books.author_english: Ali Tahawi
books.summary_english: Written by researcher Ali Tahawi in September 2018, this rigorous hadith-critical treatise is a direct refutation of Indian Ahl-e-Hadith writer Kifayatullah Sanabili's controversial book 'Yazid ibn Muawiyah Par Ilzamat Ka Tahqiqi Ja'izah'. Applying strict standards of Jarh wa Ta'dil (narrator criticism) and isnad verification, the author dismantles Sanabili's attempts to weaken authentic reports regarding Karbala and whitewash Yazid's character. He authenticates the chains of narration proving the culpability of Umar ibn Sa'd, Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, and Yazid in the martyrdom of Imam Hussain (RA), Yazid's mistreatment of the blessed head of Hussain (RA) and failure to punish the killers, the coercive nature of Yazid's nomination opposed by Abdullah ibn Umar, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and Imam Hussain (RA), and the Prophetic hadith warning that the first to alter the Sunnah would be a man from Banu Umayyah named Yazid. The book concludes by refuting Sanabili's misattribution of praise for Yazid to Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and proving Imam Layth ibn Sa'd's and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal's condemnation of Yazid, followed on pages 461–464 by the Master Index of all 54 books across the 12 volumes of Majmua Kutub Ihtisab-e-Nasbiyat.
